raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

When a model has more than one attention backend, `_preferred_block_size_for_backends` returns 16 whenever every backend accepts the default, and never calls `get_preferred_block_size`. Use the largest preferred size when every backend accepts it. Fixes #60871.

## Claims

- The largest preference replaces 16 only when every backend already accepts 16 and every backend accepts that larger size. A single backend is unchanged. If any backend rejects 16, the LCM search is unchanged.
- From declared sizes, not from end-to-end runs, that moves 16 to a larger preference for:
  - Llama-4, encoder-decoder models, and Inkling on XPU FlashAttention (16 to 64)
  - Llama-4 and cross-attention encoder-decoder on ROCm AITER unified (16 to 64)
  - a dense model with `ultraquant_4bit` and skip layers on ROCm (16 to 64)
  - Qwen4Exp with QSA on SM100, head size 256, and FA4 (16 to 128, before hybrid alignment)
- DeepSeek-V4.1 and Llama-4 with `--attention-backend B12X` stay on the current LCM result.

## Validation

`ruff` 0.14.0 format and check pass on the two changed files.

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_preferred_block_size_satisfies_every_backend tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_preferred_block_size_keeps_default_when_largest_preference_is_rejected tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_preferred_block_size_searches_past_an_exact_size_backend tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_preferred_block_size_rejects_backends_with_no_common_size
```

Result on the previous revision: 8 passed in 0.42s. This update adds one LCM pin, `([[64], ([MultipleOf(32)], 256)], 64)`, so the same command now has nine cases. `ruff` 0.14.0 was run again on the two files. The new case was not executed in that earlier run.

## Details

`Platform._preferred_block_size_for_backends` (from #49845) calls `get_preferred_block_size` only for one backend. With two or more, `supports_block_size(16)` is true for `MultipleOf(16)` and for an exact 16, so the function returns 16. That skips preferences of 64 (`FLASH_ATTN` on XPU, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`) and 128 (`HPUAttentionBackendV1`).

In-tree platforms do not crash on this. The HPU plugin does: the runner snapshots 128 before this selection overwrites the block size with 16, and prompt warmup then fails unflatten. vllm-gaudi works around it in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-gaudi/pull/1871. This change makes that workaround removable for the case where every backend accepts the larger preference.

The preference check sits inside the branch where every backend accepts the default. Putting it earlier also rewrites the LCM path: DeepSeek-V4.1 would take the SWA preference of 256 instead of 64 on SM90 and ROCm gfx942, or 128 on SM100 and SM120. Llama-4 with B12X on SM120 would move from 64 to 128. Those stay on the LCM result.

`ultraquant_attn.py` notes that decode geometry wants a block of 64, while Phase 1 currently selects 16 there. Phase 3 was not checked, so this is only an observation from the declared sizes.

#58630 changes how specs are queried. It does not apply this rule.

AI assistance was used to draft this change. The submitter reviewed the diff and ran the unit tests above.

     from vllm.v1.attention.backend import AttentionBackend
 
     class _MockBackendCls(AttentionBackend):
@@ -450,6 +453,12 @@ def get_supported_kernel_block_sizes():
             def supports_block_size(cls, block_size: int | None) -> bool:
                 return block_size is None or block_size in supported
 
+        if preferred is not None:
+
+            @classmethod
+            def get_preferred_block_size(cls, default_block_size: int) -> int:
+                return preferred
+
     return _MockBackendCls
 
 
@@ -466,13 +475,35 @@ def supports_block_size(cls, block_size: int | None) -> bool:
         ([[32, 64]], 32),
         # Neither divides the other, so only the LCM satisfies both.
         ([[32], [48]], 96),
+        # Both accept the default 16 and prefer 64, so the largest shared
+        # preference wins over 16.
+        ([([MultipleOf(16)], 64), ([MultipleOf(16)], 64)], 64),
+        # A backend that rejects 16 stays on the LCM path. Preferring 256
+        # must not replace lcm(64, 32).
+        ([[64], ([MultipleOf(32)], 256)], 64),
     ],
 )
 def test_preferred_block_size_satisfies_every_backend(backends, expected):
-    classes = [_mock_backend(s) for s in backends]
+    classes = []
+    for spec in backends:
+        if isinstance(spec, tuple):
+            supported, preferred = spec
+            classes.append(_mock_backend(supported, preferred=preferred))
+        else:
+            classes.append(_mock_backend(spec))
     assert Platform._preferred_block_size_for_backends(classes, 16, None) == expected
 
 
+def test_preferred_block_size_keeps_default_when_largest_preference_is_rejected():
+    # 128 is the larger preference, but the exact backend rejects it.
+    # Both still accept 16, so the old default path stays.
+    classes = [
+        _mock_backend([16, 32], exact=True, preferred=128),
+        _mock_backend([MultipleOf(16)], preferred=16),
+    ]
+    assert Platform._preferred_block_size_for_backends(classes, 16, None) == 16
+
+

@@ -721,6 +726,16 @@ def _preferred_block_size_for_backends(
             if len(backend_classes) == 1:
                 return backend_classes[0].get_preferred_block_size(default_block_size)
             if all(b.supports_block_size(default_block_size) for b in backend_classes):
+                # Each backend can prefer a different size. Use the largest
+                # only when every backend accepts it; otherwise the default.
+                largest_preferred = max(
+                    b.get_preferred_block_size(default_block_size)
+                    for b in backend_classes
+                )
+                if all(
